beats.intro: Money in a bank can grow on its own, and borrowed money costs extra to pay back. [[q]]That extra is called interest.
beats.terms: When you save, the bank pays you interest. When you borrow, you pay interest to the lender. [[p]]The principal is the amount you save or borrow. [[r]]The interest rate is the percent charged or paid each year. [[t]]And the time is how many years the money is saved or borrowed. [[f]]Simple interest multiplies all three: interest equals principal times rate times time. I equals P R T.
beats.grow: Let's watch it grow. [[q]]You deposit two hundred fifty dollars at three percent a year. [[y1]]After one year, you earn three percent of two fifty: seven dollars and fifty cents. [[y2]]In the second year, you earn another seven fifty, [[y3]]and in the third year, another seven fifty. [[same]]With simple interest, the interest is the same every year, because it's always three percent of the same principal. [[calc]]So after three years: two fifty times zero point zero three times three is twenty-two fifty. [[bal]]The balance, principal plus interest, is two hundred seventy-two dollars and fifty cents.
beats.months: The rate is per year, so the time must be in years too. [[m]]Eight months is eight twelfths of a year, which is two thirds. [[w]]Six weeks is six fifty-seconds of a year. [[ex]]For example, a loan of nine hundred dollars at six percent for eight months: [[calc]]nine hundred times zero point zero six times two thirds is thirty-six dollars of interest.
beats.time: The formula also works backward. [[q]]How long must four thousand dollars sit at four percent to earn six hundred dollars? [[sub]]Put in what you know: six hundred equals four thousand times zero point zero four times T. [[simp]]Four thousand times zero point zero four is one hundred sixty, so six hundred equals one sixty T. [[div]]Divide six hundred by one sixty: [[ans]]T is three point seven five years. That's three years and nine months. [[check]]Check: each year earns one hundred sixty dollars, and three and three quarter years of that is six hundred.
beats.compound: Some accounts pay compound interest instead. [[q]]Put one thousand dollars in at two percent. [[y1]]After one year, both kinds of account earn twenty dollars. [[y2s]]In the second year, simple interest earns another twenty dollars. [[y2c]]But compound interest earns two percent of the new balance, one thousand twenty dollars, which is twenty dollars and forty cents. [[gap]]The gap is small at first, but it grows every year, because compound interest earns interest on interest.
beats.wrap: Simple interest is principal times rate times time. [[w1]]Write the rate as a decimal, and the time in years. [[w2]]The balance is the principal plus the interest. [[w3]]To find a missing value, put in what you know and divide. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final2: Next, work backward to find the missing value.
